territorial_scope.description: Applies to ICTS transactions conducted by persons under US jurisdiction or involving US-jurisdiction property, reaches persons 'wherever located' in the foreign-adversary definition, and final determinations target specific transactions.

evidence.quote: Is conducted by any person subject to the jurisdiction of the United States or involves property subject to the jurisdiction of the United States

summary.short: Commerce rule implementing Executive Order 13873 on procedures for reviewing and prohibiting or mitigating information and communications technology transactions involving foreign-adversary-linked persons. Covers listed ICTS, including AI and machine learning, for transactions on or after January 19, 2021, with IEEPA penalties.
summary.long: Subpart A defines scope: ICTS transactions, initiated on or after January 19, 2021 and subject to US jurisdiction, involving products or services designed or supplied by persons tied to foreign adversaries (designated in §7.4). Covered categories include critical infrastructure, telecommunications networks, data hosting handling sensitive personal data on over one million US persons, widely sold devices and used software, and ICTS integral to artificial intelligence and machine learning, quantum, drones, autonomous systems or robotics. Subpart B sets review procedures: referral, initial review against listed risk criteria, interagency consultation, an initial determination, a 30-day response window, and a final determination (prohibited, not prohibited, or permitted with mitigation), generally within 180 days. The Secretary may require sworn information and record retention, and keeps submissions confidential subject to exceptions. Subpart C sets penalties: civil penalties up to the greater of $250,000 (inflation-adjusted) or twice the transaction value; criminal fines up to $1,000,000 and imprisonment up to 20 years for willful violations; administrative penalties up to $307,922 (inflation-adjusted) or twice the transaction value per violation.

notes: The provided text is Part 7, Subparts A to C, of the ICTS supply chain rule under Executive Order 13873. The registry title refers to connected vehicles, but the text does not mention vehicles; scope rests on the § 7.3(a)(4) ICTS categories. No Federal Register preamble is included. Internal points: § 7.200(a)(1) gives IEEPA's maximum civil penalty as the greater of $250,000 (subject to inflation) or twice the transaction amount, while § 7.200(a)(3) gives an inflation-adjusted figure of $307,922; both are in the text and belong to enforcement. Several subsections carry duplicated labels such as '(c) (c)', '(d) (d)' and '(f) (f)', apparently formatting artifacts. Definitional references to other law (e.g., 48 CFR 2.101, 15 CFR 772.1, 19 CFR 201.6, 15 U.S.C. 1681a) are not coded as relations.
